accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS 4.OA.1 (interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5) and 4.OA.2 (multiplicative comparison word problems with a symbol for the unknown, distinguished from additive comparison), the Common Core Progressions document for Operations and Algebraic Thinking K-5 (Table 2 comparison situations, bigger unknown and smaller unknown, tape diagrams), and the National Curriculum in England Year 4 multiplication aims on integer scaling problems. Every number in the lab, items and challenge was recomputed: 4 × 3 = 12, 36 ÷ 4 = 9, 40 ÷ 5 = 8, 42 ÷ 6 = 7, 12 × 6 = 72, 48 ÷ 6 = 8, 20 ÷ 5 = 4, and for 1 the sum 1 + 4 = 5 beats 4 × 1 = 4.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips named in the OA Progressions and Nunes and Bryant's research on additive versus multiplicative reasoning: adding when the text says times as many (prediction 1 option 7, challenge 'add', m7 distractor 18 kg), reading the equation backwards so the smaller number is the one that is times as many ('swap', p2, m3), subtracting to find a smaller unknown (prediction 4 option 32, 'sub', m6), multiplying when the unknown is the smaller amount (prediction 4 option 144, 'mult'), dividing when the larger amount is unknown ('div'), and believing times as many is always bigger than more (prediction 2, 'bigger', p5, m10).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtimesas is about one quantity being copies of another: Sara's bar is dragged cell by cell over four dashed copies of Tom's 3 and labelled with how many whole copies it holds; a three-bar race shows t + 4 against 4 × t for Tom amounts 1 to 6 so the crossover at 1 is seen; a 35 bar regroups between 5 sevens and 7 fives while four statements are judged; a draggable unknown bar is copied k times over 36, 40 and 42 until it fits; and four sentences are matched to an equation with a bar model drawn for each. flagttfam builds times-table facts and fact families, flagratio mixes part-to-part ratios. lab_distinct passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers before being told: dragging Sara to 7 triggers 'that is 4 more, not 4 times'; choosing Tom = 1 shows 4 more beating 4 times; tapping the 35 bar shows both groupings are the same total; letting go of the unknown bar at 32 says it treats times as more and shows 4 × 32 = 128 is far too big; picking an adding equation for a times sentence names why multiplication is needed.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 7 or 4 for 4 times as many as 3 (the bar needs 12 cells to fill four copies), '4 times as many' for Tom = 1 (the bars show 5 against 4), and 32 or 144 for the unknown in 36 = 4 × n (the copies overflow or fall short until n = 9).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions and seven distinct feedback messages naming the slip: adding instead of multiplying, dividing when the bigger amount is unknown, reading times as more, swapping which number is times as many, taking away instead of dividing, multiplying when the unknown is the smaller amount, and assuming times is always bigger. Answer order rotates.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 1.9 with short sentences built around one story (Tom's 3 stickers); adult text averages 7.1 with the standards named. Bar labels state the arithmetic (4 more than Tom: 3 + 4 = 7; 4 times as many as Tom: 4 × 3 = 12) so the meaning is read off the picture.

no_filler.evidence: Gate finds no filler. Each kid paragraph carries one idea (copies, more versus times, reading an equation both ways, finding a hidden amount). Items vary contexts and directions: marbles and ribbons for a bigger unknown, a tree and a shed for a smaller unknown, how many more after a times comparison (m5), two crates (m9), and spotting Eva's subtraction slip (m6).

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of every step: light theme at the start and after Show me finished, dark theme mid-way and after finishing. The first dark pass hid the group outlines (dark ink on dark bars), so outlines now switch to near-white in dark theme; the solved Find and Write steps were blank on finishing and now keep the last bar model and the green equation on screen. 24- and 42-cell bars fit 390 px; buttons wrap to two or three rows.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: −1, +1 and Add a copy of Tom; Tom has 1 to Tom has 6; True, False and Regroup the bar; −1, +1 and Check for the unknown; one button per equation. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with each result (how many copies Sara has, which comparison is bigger, why a card is true or false, whether the copies fit). walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
